### Fixed

- Every upgrade asked the keychain once for each secret it read, twenty
  secrets being twenty dialogs. A keychain item trusts the signature of the
  program that stored it, and the release binary was signed ad-hoc, which is
  a signature made of the binary's own hash, so each release was a stranger to
  the items the one before it had stored. The macOS binary is now signed with
  a Developer ID, the same identity from one release to the next. This release
  asks once more for each item, and Always Allow is the last answer an upgrade
  needs.

### Documentation

- [What the keychain
  asks](https://docs.monk3ys.dev/docs/concepts/vault/#what-the-keychain-asks):
  the page said nothing, which was wrong. It now says when the keychain asks,
  and why a build from source asks again after each rebuild.
